phase.label: Jasrota, in the service of Balwant Singh, c. 1740–63

source.label: Wikipedia: “Around 1740 he left the family workshop in Guler and moved to Jasrota … This is the best known and documented phase of his career”
Wikipedia: paintings by Nainsukh “show the raja … writing a letter”
Wikipedia: “Nainsukh was a famous master of the mid-18th century, followed by his family workshop”

work.text: In his naturalistic depiction of buildings and books and his efforts to depict depth, Nainsukh shows the influence of his study of works by Mughal painters.

moment.text: The most intimate Pahari portraitures of rulers are those of Raja Balwant Singh of Jasrota, Raja Sidh Sen and Raja Shamsher Sen of Mandi, and Raja Chattar Singh of Chamba.

matters.text: Balwant Singh must have lacked the normal attitude of other Indian royalty to only allow images to be produced that displayed the magnificence of his life; who between patron and painter first suggested this very informal approach is unknown.
When Balwant Singh had to spend a period in exile in Guler Nainsukh accompanied him.
